  "aggregated_raw_content": "The Senate Banking Committee has voted to advance the Clarity Act, a key piece of cryptocurrency legislation, to a full Senate vote.

Senate Democrats splintered Thursday in their support of the Clarity Act during the crucial vote, with two pro-crypto members of the party voting for the landmark crypto bill, and all others voting against.

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) voted for the legislation, despite the fact both had indicated they would not do so unless a deal on language related to limiting President Donald Trump’s personal crypto ventures had been met by the time of today’s vote. No such deal has yet been reached.

During the Senate Banking hearing, all Republican committee members joined Gallego and Alsobrooks to support the bill, which now moves to the Senate floor for final consideration. If passed and signed into law by President Trump, the Clarity Act would formally legalize most crypto activity in the United States.

The bill will need support from at least seven Democrats on the Senate floor to ultimately pass.

An Alsobrooks spokesperson previously told Decrypt the senator would only vote for the Clarity Act at committee if "a substantive agreement on ethics" was struck.

When reached after today’s vote, the spokesperson told Decrypt Alsobrooks voted yes "because of the good faith negotiations that have transpired," and added the senator "will continue negotiating on ethics specifically."

At the hearing, Gallego qualified his "yes" vote by saying it may change in the future if an ethics deal regarding the president isn’t reached.

"We have come close, but not finished, an agreement on ethics guardrails for elected officials—all elected officials," Gallego said.

"If this is not resolved by the time of the floor [vote], like I have in the past, I am not afraid to vote no," he added.

President Trump and his family have invested in numerous crypto ventures since his 2024 re-election campaign. The president co-founded a crypto firm, World Liberty Financial, which has gone on to make lucrative deals with foreign nations, and, just days before his inauguration, launched a meme coin which surged to a valuation of nearly 0 billion before crashing in value.

Just last month, Trump hosted top holders of the meme coin at Mar-a-Lago for a private gala where he discussed the Iran war, among other subjects.

Gallego and Alsobrooks’ splintering from other pro-crypto Democrats on the Banking Committee, who all voted no today, followed warnings from crypto industry watchdog Stand With Crypto, which earlier this week announced it would score lawmakers based on today’s vote.

Coinbase is a key backer of Fairshake, a crypto super PAC that plans to spend over 00 million on November’s midterm elections.

Gallego and Alsobrooks both currently enjoy sterling "A" ratings from Stand With Crypto, and Fairshake spent heavily to back Gallego’s upstart Senate campaign in 2024.

"Stand With Crypto scored senators’ votes on the Banking Committee markup and will incorporate these into lawmakers’ scores… so that every voter can understand where elected officials stand on crypto priorities," the organization said in a statement shared with Decrypt following today’s vote.

Procedural drama defined today’s Senate Banking hearing, with committee chairman Tim Scott (R-SC) refusing to hold votes on certain amendments to the Clarity Act that would have proven uncomfortable for his Republican colleagues.

One such amendment would have forced lawmakers to choose a side in a long-running feud between the banking lobby and the crypto industry over yield on stablecoins, cryptocurrencies pegged to the value of the U.S. dollar. Another would have likely seen Republicans vote down changes to the bill’s provisions on decentralized finance requested by law enforcement.

Making matters more tense was the fact Scott claimed he was preventing those votes due to a technical drafting error—but then proceeded to hold a vote on other amendments with the same drafting issues.

"I am deeply concerned that law enforcement officials… [and] community banks will listen to this and wonder why their point of view just couldn’t be heard," Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), the Banking Committee’s top Democrat, said during the skirmish.

*Editor's note: This story was updated after publication to include additional details.*

Cointelegraph reported that Santiment warned the crypto market "typically" moves against crowd expectations, pointing to a recent rise in bullish sentiment driven by renewed momentum around the US CLARITY Act.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC) is trading at 9,084 at the time of publication, up 3.15% since May 1, according to CoinMarketCap.

Santiment reported that there are currently 1.55 bullish social media comments on Bitcoin for every bearish comment, suggesting this sentiment skew may be flashing warning signs. "We advise caution. Markets typically move opposite to the crowd’s expectations at all times," Santiment said.

However, crypto analysts are staying optimistic that the trend will continue. MN Trading Capital founder Michael van de Poppe said in an X post on Friday that the legislation is "the biggest, and historical, bill for the entire industry and can be a strong trigger for the upcoming bull market."

White House crypto advisor Patrick Witt said in an X post on Friday that while the CLARITY Act vote was "a major step forward," it is not yet finalized.

"As Senators on both sides of the dais noted, there’s more work to be done before this legislation is ready for prime time. We’ll keep working in good faith to build the support needed to pass the bill on the Senate floor," Witt said.

Santiment said any movement towards the CLARITY Act’s passage "can and should be considered bullish for crypto (in the long run) because it could finally give the industry clearer rules in the United States."

"If the CLARITY Act passes, more institutional money and powerful players would be expected to enter (or re-enter) the markets," Santiment said.

However, the sentiment platform warned that the largest cryptocurrencies could be "baked in" before the CLARITY Act is officially passed.

Other metrics suggest market participants are becoming more cautious about the broader crypto market. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which measures overall crypto market sentiment, posted a "Fear" score of 31 on Saturday.",

# CLARITY Act advances with 1.55-to-1 Bitcoin sentiment

clarity act momentum is now a live market input after the Senate Banking Committee advanced the bill to a full Senate vote. The move matters because it puts a formal U.S. market structure framework closer to the floor, where the bill will still need at least seven Democratic votes to pass.

Traders reacted fast. Santiment said Bitcoin social chatter flipped to 1.55 bullish comments for every bearish one, while Bitcoin stayed up 3.15% from May 1 and broader sentiment showed a sharp rise in optimism tied to the vote.

This does not look like blind risk-on buying. It looks like traders repricing the odds of clearer U.S. rules, while still respecting the political risk ahead.

## Crypto market structure bill and bitcoin sentiment: What the vote signals

The first signal is political, not technical. [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/coindesk-news/2026/05/15/crypto-market-structure-bill-clears-key-hurdle-as-ethics-debate-looms-over-floor-vote) that the Senate Banking Committee advanced the CLARITY Act after clearing a key bipartisan checkpoint, which gives the market a real legislative milestone instead of another headline with no follow-through.

The second signal is behavioral. [Cointelegraph reported](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-clarity-act-brings-major-spike-of-euphoria-to-bitcoin-santiment) that Santiment saw a major spike of euphoria as the bill moved forward, but also warned that markets often lean against crowded expectations when bullish positioning becomes too obvious.

[CHART_PLACEHOLDER]

### Why the committee vote matters

Committee approval does not finish the process, but it changes the map. The bill is now closer to a full Senate test, and that is where crypto traders will start pricing actual vote math instead of general policy hopes.

The split inside the Democratic caucus is the key detail. [Decrypt reported](https://decrypt.co/367871/democrats-split-clarity-act-crypto-bill-passes-senate-committee-vote) that Senators Ruben Gallego and Angela Alsobrooks voted yes alongside all Republican members, even though ethics language tied to President Trump’s crypto business activity had not yet been finalized.

That matters because the market got proof of bipartisan traction, but not proof of final passage.

- The bill cleared committee with Republican support plus two Democratic votes.
- Ethics negotiations are still open and could affect floor support.
- The Senate floor will require a broader Democratic coalition than the committee vote did.

### Why traders are not treating this as a done deal

Gallego made the near-term risk plain. He said his support could change if ethics guardrails are not resolved before the floor vote. Alsobrooks' office also framed the committee vote as part of continuing good-faith negotiations, not a blank check.

That keeps the CLARITY Act in a tradable but unfinished zone. Bulls can argue the bill has real momentum, while skeptics can point to the same facts and say the hardest vote has not happened yet.

There was also procedural tension in committee. Chair Tim Scott declined votes on some amendments that would have created tougher choices for Republicans, including issues around stablecoin yield and decentralized finance provisions requested by law enforcement. Elizabeth Warren criticized that handling, which shows this bill still carries policy friction even after the headline win.

## Key Bitcoin price levels traders should watch now

The next move in bitcoin price may depend less on the headline itself and more on whether positioning has already run too far. The market has a bullish legislative narrative, but the supporting signals are mixed once sentiment and risk appetite are separated.

[CHART_PLACEHOLDER]

### 1.55 bullish-to-bearish sentiment is the first signal

Santiment’s 1.55-to-1 reading is useful because it measures crowd conviction in real time. When the ratio gets stretched, upside can continue for a while, but the trade becomes easier to fade if new buyers stop showing up.

For traders, this means the CLARITY Act headline should be paired with positioning discipline. A strong narrative plus crowded optimism can still produce a pullback, especially if senators start signaling that ethics language remains unresolved or if the floor timeline slips.

### Fear and floor-vote math remain the second signal

The broader Crypto Fear & Greed Index sat at 31, which is still in Fear territory. That creates an unusual setup: Bitcoin-specific chatter turned bullish, but the wider market has not fully confirmed the move.

This gap is worth watching because it can cut two ways. If broader sentiment catches up, bitcoin price could extend higher on fresh participation. If it does not, the current euphoria can fade into a choppy reaction trade rather than a clean trend leg.

Look for:
- updates on whether at least seven Democrats are moving toward a floor-vote yes
- whether bullish Bitcoin commentary keeps rising or starts cooling from the 1.55 ratio
- whether broader market sentiment climbs out of Fear and confirms the move

## Conclusion

The clarity act has moved from policy discussion to active market catalyst, with the committee vote and the 1.55 bullish-to-bearish Bitcoin sentiment ratio now setting the tone.

Near term, the setup is constructive but not clean. Traders have a positive regulatory headline, yet they also have unresolved ethics negotiations, uncertain Senate floor math, and crowd optimism that may already be running ahead of itself.

Watch the vote count, not just the headlines. If floor support broadens and broader market sentiment firms up, the move can build. If those pieces stall, treat strength as event-driven and stay selective.

## FAQs

**1. Why did clarity act momentum move the market?**  
The committee vote gave traders a concrete sign that U.S. crypto legislation is progressing instead of stalling. That matters because the bill could create clearer rules for market structure in the United States. When that prospect gets closer, Bitcoin often reacts first because it is the market’s main risk barometer.

**2. Is this the start of a bigger rally?**  
It could be, but the signal is not confirmed yet. The bullish case is that clearer regulation can pull in more institutional participation over time. The caution case is that sentiment already looks crowded, and the bill still needs a tougher Senate floor vote before traders can treat it as settled.

**3. What levels or signals should traders watch now?**  
The main signals are not just price marks. Traders should watch the 1.55 bullish-to-bearish social ratio, the Crypto Fear & Greed reading of 31, and signs that Senate Democrats are moving toward a floor-vote deal. If those metrics improve together, the trade looks healthier.

**4. How does this affect the broader crypto market?**  
A strong CLARITY Act push can help the whole market because it reduces policy uncertainty around U.S. crypto activity. That can support Bitcoin first, then spill into majors and selected altcoins. But if the bill gets delayed or diluted, the broader market may lose momentum quickly.

**5. What is the historical context for this move?**  
Crypto has rallied before on hopes of regulatory clarity, but those moves often fade when legislation runs into political resistance. What is different here is that the bill cleared a meaningful committee hurdle with bipartisan support. What has not changed is that final passage still depends on difficult vote math.

**6. What are the short-term risks for investors?**  
The biggest risk is assuming the committee vote guarantees passage. Ethics concerns tied to Trump-linked crypto ventures are still being negotiated, and some senators have left room to change their position. The other risk is sentiment getting too bullish too fast, which can invite a reversal if expectations outrun progress.
